I would normally initially ask you to contact myself directly to discuss any issues you have with us but in this case I believe we had already spoken about this specific point. 
As an aside, in way of reply, we genuinely try our best to help the needs of our patient population but we can only work within the remit of the NHS, and this includes the prescribing of medicines.
Certain medications fall outside of the remit of primary care prescribing, and can only be issued by GPs under the umbrella of shared care agreements. These agreements have mandated clauses set by our governing body, GM ICB and we follow these in order to remain safe and compliant with strict regulations on prescribing.

Staff are very friendly and helpful. Online form is easy to fill out and I usually get a response on the same day or the morning after.
However one thing that is really annoying is the travel vaccinations appointments. I don’t understand how I can get a doctor to call me the next day for a non urgent appointment but I cant book a *TELEPHONE*  travel vaccination appointment for a whole month. With my previous experience from different practices, an easier and more efficient way is filling a detailed form with where I’m travelling to, duration of trip, previous medical history, previous vaccination with the ability to add evidence, any drug allergies, any previous reactions or allergies to vaccinations, etc. A full risk assessment via the form instead of a telephone call that needs to be booked in and the next availability for that would be over a month.
Then, I’m sure the scheduling of the practice nurses, nursing assistants/associates, advanced nurse practitioners, etc can be organised better to fit in travel vaccination appointment based on the risk assessment form and the date when the patient is traveling. I'm happy to discuss this with you personally if you want to get in touch but in the interim, please accept my replies here. 
We acknowledge that travel appointments have a longer lead time, and this is due to the fact we have 1 dedicated member of staff for this service, as opposed to the multiple clinicians employed by the practice, with finite NHS budget to do so, to prioritise the acute needs of patients presenting with health complications.
This does mean that we have made an active decision to use the funding available towards maintaining the 24hr service for acute needs and I understand that this has led to a disappointment for yourself with your travel appointment needs. 
Regarding your suggestions that we should reallocate booked appointments based on travel date - we would politely decline this alternative option as this would not be fair to the patient who has booked their appointment in good time prior to travelling.

We always look to improve in areas where we can and take feedback seriously. Within the financial envelope offered to us by the NHS, we have to make business decisions which can result in levels of dissatisfaction in certain areas but I believe we have made the right one now to prioritise same day access to GP appointments in a landscape where this is often not the case.

It becomes even more challenging for those of us with multiple health issues requiring separate appointments for each issue.  I recently had my flu vaccine a couple of Saturdays ago but I also need to attend appointments for; diabetic screening, liver blood test and 3 courses of hepatitis jabs.  I wonder why several issues can`t be dealt with during one appointment which would help me immensely when trying to balance my shift work with attending multiple GP appointments requiring me to find a parking spot and then pay for said parking on multiple occasions.

Thank you for the in-depth review and taking the time to review the service. Feedback is essential for us and I'm so very glad to read and absorb your comments and experiences. 
I've got a few suggestions that might help going forward. You're completely correct that shift workers often face difficulties pre-planning appointments but you should know that we ALWAYS have nursing appointments available at the weekend with less than 1 week notice so therefore you would always be able to get an appointment this way without having to cancel. Regarding weekdays, we offer evening appointments but are very much limited for phlebotomy due to the laboratories picking up the last samples at 4pm. We do however offer 8am appointments for those patients who may be unable to attend during the day. 
For GP appointments, you will always be offered an option for a call or a face to face within 24hrs of request so you should not need to try to plan for these 3 weeks in advance. 
I've also noted your comments regarding multiple appointments. We can often combine appointments for multiple reasons but for example, dedicated flu clinics only have 2 min appointment slots and therefore patients requiring additional services would need to book separate appointments for these outside of this clinic.
I hope I've been able to clarify or help in some way but if you ever want to feed back directly, I'm always available to speak to patients should they wish. Dee Turner, Practice Business patient, I am sorry to hear of your experience and would happily discuss this with you if you are happy to contact the surgery to discuss. Unfortunately some clinics do run late and we do our best to keep patients informed if this is the case.
